A spherical balloon is inflated so that its radius increases at a rate of $1\,\text{cm/s}.$ How fast is the volume of the balloon increasing at the moment when the radius is $2\,\text{cm}?$

activity_context.topic_title: Calculating Related Rates With Circles and Spheres

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14095273/assets/e13f4de3d3d66ba1205b3da8cbe8abec300a94d2e53453af3c9c12667e1d7907.png)

A spherical soap bubble is expanding, causing its enclosed volume to increase at a rate of $24\pi \text{ }{\text{cm}}^{3}/\text{s}.$ How fast is the radius increasing at the moment when the radius is $3\text{ }\text{cm}?$ Do not round the answer.

The radius of the bubble is increasing at a rate of 
{{field-1}} $\text{cm}/\text{s}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $r$ be the radius of the bubble and $V$ its volume. Both $r$ and $V$ change with time. In particular, we are given

$$
\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t}=24\pi \,{\text{cm}}^{3}/\text{s},
$$

and we want to find $\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}$ when $r=3\,\text{cm}.$

To start, let's write down the formula for the volume of a sphere and then differentiate it using implicit differentiation. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\frac{4}{3}\pi {r}^{3} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(V) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{4}{3}\pi {r}^{3}) \\ \frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}r}(\frac{4}{3}\pi {r}^{3}) \\ \frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}\cdot 4\pi {r}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now we can substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t}=24\pi $ and $r=3,$ and solve for $\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}24\pi  & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}\cdot 4\pi (3)^{2} \\ 24\pi  & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}\cdot 36\pi  \\ \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, when the radius is of the bubble is $3\,\text{cm},$ the radius is increasing at a rate of  $\frac{2}{3}$ $\text{ }\,\text{cm}/\text{s}.$
